verdict.rationale: Better Auth is a self-hosted library that stores user data in a database you configure yourself (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and more). Users confirm all auth data lives in their own DB with no provider lock-in, so storage location follows wherever you host that database. However, the docs never address region selection or data residency directly; residency is an implicit result of the bring-your-own-database design, not a dedicated control. Missing for 10: explicit residency/region documentation, any first-party data-residency guidance or controls, independent corroboration specifically about residency.
